key_insight: A Rabi drive applied during dispersive readout makes the computational qubit states effectively indistinguishable while keeping leakage states detectable, enabling heralded leakage detection without destroying the stored quantum information.
engineering_relevance: This provides a hardware-minimal way to flag leakage errors in superconducting processors, improving compatibility with error-correction workflows on fixed-frequency transmons and related qubit platforms.
method: Drive the computational transition during resonator readout.
Suppress state discrimination within the |0⟩, |1⟩ subspace while preserving contrast for |2⟩ and higher states.
Condition downstream processing on the no-leakage measurement outcome.
evidence_signal: The method achieved 97.1(3)% leakage-detection fidelity in an 80-ns window, with a 2.3(3)% false-flag rate from the computational subspace and 92.9(5)% average post-detection state fidelity for an equal mixture of computational and leakage populations.
watch_item: Performance depends on carefully tuned drive and readout conditions, so leakage rejection and preserved coherence may be sensitive to calibration drift and device-specific parameters.
paper_title: Heralded Leakage Detection with Preserved Computational-State Coherence in a Fixed-Frequency Transmon
